title: Data analyst
summary: SQL and Python with pandas, from the first query to cleaned, joined, charted and modelled data that answers a business question.
outcome: Ready to take a question from a stakeholder, pull the data with SQL, clean and analyse it in pandas, and present a chart and a caveated answer.

stages.title: SQL first
stages.why: Most company data sits in a database, and SQL is the one tool every analyst team shares. Filtering, aggregation, joins, CTEs and window functions answer most questions on their own.
stages.milestone: Answers a business question with one readable query: joins, grouping and a running total

stages.title: Python for analysis
stages.why: Python picks up where SQL stops: files, APIs, reshaping and statistics. Enough of the language to read and write notebook code with confidence.
stages.milestone: Writes small Python functions that read a file and summarise it

stages.title: pandas: shape, clean, join
stages.why: Real data is messy. Most analysis time goes into types, missing values, duplicates and joins, and doing that reproducibly is what makes a result trustworthy.
stages.milestone: Turns a messy export into a clean, joined table and a sales summary someone can act on

stages.title: Time and pictures
stages.why: Most business questions are about change over time, and most answers are a chart. Resampling, rolling windows and honest charts that do not mislead.
stages.milestone: Builds a weekly trend chart from a warehouse table and explains the seasonality

stages.title: Statistics and first models
stages.why: "Did the change work?" needs more than two averages. Distributions, confidence and a first regression, with the caveats a careful analyst states.
stages.milestone: Tests whether a difference is real and fits a model with a fair train/test split

stages.title: A professional workflow
stages.why: Analysis others can rerun beats a one-off notebook. Idiomatic Python, tests, Git and regex for the text clean-up that every dataset needs.
stages.milestone: Ships an analysis as a tested script in Git that a colleague can rerun next month
